segments: From the Chronography of Barhebraeus.

They, however, that very night,
loaded their horses,
and took countless goods,
and set out that very night.
And when morning dawned,
not even one of them was left behind;
only their place was seen.
And in the year one thousand five hundred and ninety-nine [1288 AD],
in the month of Nisan,
there was some dispute between the Kurds and the Mongols who were near them,
and the Mongols conceived a grudge against them.
And while they were setting out,
six men of them remained behind,
and went and hid along the road to Mosul.
And then {OCR?}, when twelve illustrious men from among the inhabitants of Beth Khudida were coming,
those accursed ones fell upon them,
and slaughtered them all like sheep without mercy,
in broad daylight when the sun was in the dome of heaven.
And after an hour others came from Mosul,
and found those wronged ones wallowing in their blood,
while breath still remained in one of them.
And they carried him and brought him to the village.
And he recounted to them how they had been killed,
and the names of the pagan murderers.
And after three days he also died.
After the kingdom was established for Arghun, son of Abaqa,
Buqa the treasurer, who had been the cause of deliverance for Arghun from Ahmad,
as was shown above,
was glorified and became exceedingly great in the kingdom,
to such a degree
that the sons of kings and queens,
and sons-in-law and daughters-in-law,
and commanders of the Mongol armies,
would come to pay him homage,
and would stand at his door,
and demand rations {or allowances} from him.
And all the administration of the kingdom was committed to him,
and the kings and governors of all the countries under the dominion of the house of Magog,
apart from his command and the red seal belonging to Buqa,
were not received.
And this same Buqa appointed his brother Aruq as general chief and commander in all the countries of Babel, Azerbaijan, and Mesopotamia.
And this man was feared and dreaded by all the Mongol forces,
and by the kings, sultans, and scribes in all these countries.
So these two brothers administered the Mongol kingdom in great prosperity and triumph ... {OCR?}
